title.value: Exploring trust development in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers: A scoping review of the literature
title.justification: The title clearly states the primary focus of the paper, which is to explore how trust is developed in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers through a review of existing literature.
title.quote: Exploring trust development in families of children towards surgical and emergency care providers: A scoping review of the literature

extractions.description: This paper reviews existing literature to identify the factors that foster trust development in pediatric surgical and urgent care settings, examining constructs like competence, communication, dependability, and caring. It highlights the importance of communication and compassionate care in building trust, especially considering sociodemographic factors like ethnicity, education, and language barriers.

primary_category.justification: The paper is not related to eco-responsible AI or environmental themes. It focuses on trust development in healthcare, specifically in pediatric surgical and emergency contexts, which does not align with any provided eco-responsible categories.
primary_category.quote: Trust is central to the therapeutic relationship between patients and their providers, yet little is known about how it is developed in the unique context of children facing surgical emergencies.

secondary_categories.justification: Since the primary focus is on healthcare and trust in pediatric surgical settings, it does not relate to any secondary eco-responsible categories either. There are no links to climate change, pollution, or sustainability topics within the provided categories.
secondary_categories.quote: We sought to identify factors fostering trust development, gaps, and areas for improvement in the context of children facing surgical emergencies.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fall under any sub-category of eco-responsible fields. Its focus is healthcare-related trust development rather than environmental or sustainable themes.
primary_sub_category.quote: Improving communication and providing compassionate care, as well as encouraging a patient-centered approach, appear to be most effective in promoting trust in pediatric surgical and urgent settings.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Due to the paper's focus on healthcare rather than on eco-responsible topics, there are no applicable sub-categories under the eco-responsible classifications.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our findings can guide future educational interventions towards strengthening parental trust and promoting child- and family-centered care in pediatric surgical settings.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper extensively explores the development of trust in healthcare settings, which does not fit into existing eco-responsible categories but aligns more with healthcare studies.
new_primary_category.quote: Trust is a central component of the relationship between patients and their physicians. In the context of the patient-physician relationship, trust can be defined as the patient's acceptance of a vulnerable situation and, as a result, their confidence that the physician will care for them.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: As the paper focuses on trust between patients and healthcare providers, a new sub-category that encompasses these themes would be 'Trust Development in Healthcare'.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Trust affects a variety of patient behaviors and attitudes such as the patient's willingness to seek medical care and reveal delicate information.
